questions.question: Describe how nomadic herders such as the Tuareg live in the Sahara.
questions.expected_answer: Nomadic herders move from place to place with their camels, goats and sheep, travelling between wells and oases to find water and grazing. They live in tents made of animal skins or woven goat hair that can be carried by camels, and eat food mostly from their animals, as well as dates and grain traded at oases. They wear long, loose robes and head coverings that let air move and protect them from sun and sand. In the past, they led camel caravans carrying salt across the Sahara.

questions.question: Explain how the San survived as hunter-gatherers in the Kalahari.
questions.expected_answer: San men hunted antelope with bows and poisoned arrows and were skilled trackers, while women gathered roots, berries, nuts and insects. They found water in roots and tsamma melons, sucked water from damp sand through hollow reeds, and stored water in ostrich eggshells buried in the sand. They built simple shelters from branches and grass and wore skin clothing. Today most San live in settled communities.

questions.question: Describe how people live at oases and in modern desert cities.
questions.expected_answer: At oases, settled farmers use underground water from wells and channels to grow date palms, vegetables and grain, and live in houses with thick mud-brick walls, small windows and flat roofs. In modern desert cities such as Cairo, Riyadh, Dubai and Phoenix, people use air conditioning, pump water from deep underground or far away and sometimes remove salt from sea water. People work in mining, tourism and solar power, such as the plants near Upington.
